sections.h2: What does the Arenac County Register of Deeds do for a home seller?
sections.html:
The Register of Deeds in Standish files the paper trail of Arenac County real estate: deeds, mortgages, discharges and the other instruments that move or burden land. For a seller, it is the office that turns a signed deed into a public record, and it is also the counter where state and county transfer tax get collected. You can reach the office at (989) 846-9201.

Its web page invites owners to sign up for land notifications, an alert service that sends an email when a new document is recorded against a property. A person who inherited a house, or who owns a place that sits empty for part of the year, may want that watch in place before listing.

Arenac is small. It is the third-smallest county in Michigan by land area, and the register's workload follows: an estimated 9,615 housing units spread along the Saginaw Bay shore and the inland river valleys.

sections.h2: What is the recording fee schedule in Arenac County?
sections.html:
Every document filed in Arenac County pays $30.00, however many pages it has. The county cites MCL 600.2657 and says the flat fee took effect on October 1, 2016.

When one document assigns or discharges more than a single instrument, the office adds $3.00 for each instrument beyond the first. A payoff release that clears two recorded mortgages, for example, would cost $36.00 to file.

Recording and transfer tax rates posted by the Arenac County Register of Deeds
ChargeRate
Recording any document$30.00 flat
Each added instrument assigned or discharged$3.00
County transfer tax$0.55 per $500 or fraction
State transfer tax$3.75 per $500 or fraction
Transfer tax applies when the value is$100 or more

sections.h2: What would transfer tax run on an Arenac County house?
sections.html:
Add the county's 55 cents to the state's $3.75 and a sale pays $4.30 per $500 of price, with a leftover partial $500 counted as a whole one. Census data for 2020 to 2024 puts the median owner-occupied value in Arenac County at $150,600. That is 302 blocks of $500, so the tax would come to $1,298.60. Your sale will be taxed on its own price.

The register's page lays out the paperwork. The deed should show the property's value. A real estate valuation affidavit can be filed in its place at no charge, provided the deed says an affidavit is being filed. The statutes the office cites for this are MCL 207.511 and 207.525.

  • The office collects the tax unless the deed qualifies for a state exemption, a county exemption, or both.
  • The deed has to name the exemption, with the statute behind it (MCL 207.505 for the county, MCL 207.526 for the state).
  • Exemptions under the state act reach gifts to a child or grandchild, foreclosure transfers, and deeds that only confirm title the buyer already holds.

sections.h2: Can you search Arenac County deeds online?
sections.html:
Yes, with two separate tools. The county's online records site covers documents from February 11, 1991 forward, and it lets you search and buy copies of filings from 1992 to the present. Older index books are handled differently.

For anything before 1992, the office points researchers to RECORDhub. You make an account, pick one of the subscription plans Arenac County offers, and then view and print pages from deed books 1 through 214. That archive is how a family finds the chain of ownership on a farm or a lakeshore lot that has not changed hands for decades.

Online searching tells you what is on file, but it does not replace a title search. If a seller spots an old easement, a lien or a name that does not match the deed, a title company can sort out what it means before a buyer's lender does.

sections.h2: Who handles property tax bills in Arenac County?
sections.html:
Ask the treasurer of the city, village or township where the parcel sits for the current tax bill, and ask the Arenac County Treasurer about any amount that has fallen behind. Each can give you a written figure to hand the closing agent.

At a sale, an unpaid tax balance is normally settled out of the seller's proceeds at the closing table. On an older or inherited house, request the payoff early, so the number you plan around matches the one the closing agent sees.

Arenac's register does not handle tax collection, so questions about assessments or exemptions go to the local assessor or treasurer rather than to the deeds counter.

sections.h2: What does the Arenac County landscape mean for a house sale?
sections.html:
Arenac County covers 681 square miles, and 47 percent of that is water, mostly Saginaw Bay on Lake Huron. Standish is the county seat and the biggest of the three cities, joined by Au Gres and Omer and Sterling, Turner and Twining as villages. The county has a start-and-stop past: the Michigan Territory created it in 1831, it was attached to Saginaw County for administration in 1836, and the creation of Bay County legally erased it in April 1857. It came back on April 21, 1883, carved from Bay County's northern townships. Anyone tracing an old Arenac farm deed should expect the records to reflect that history.

Several rivers cross the county, including the Au Gres, the Rifle and the Pine. I-75 and US 23 are the main routes, along with M-13, M-33, M-61 and M-65. Off-reservation trust land of the Isabella Indian Reservation sits in three small parcels inside Standish Township.

  • Population estimate for 2025: 15,068, a rise of 0.5 percent over 2020.
  • Households: 6,552, with 86.2 percent in owner-occupied homes.
  • Median household income: $58,811, and median gross rent: $761.
  • Share of residents 65 or older: 30.0 percent.
  • Residential and other building permits in 2025: 43.

Against a median home value near $150,600, repair costs weigh heavily on a sale. A house that needs a roof, a furnace or a cleanout can suit a cash buyer who takes it in current condition.

sections.h2: What does the Arenac County economy look like around a house sale?
sections.html:
Arenac County is a place of small employers and long commutes. The Census Bureau counts 355 employer establishments with 3,619 workers in 2023, a gain of 6.9 percent over 2022, and an annual payroll of about $169 million. Workers who travel to a job spend a mean of 26.6 minutes getting there.

The shoreline adds a visitor trade. Accommodation and food service sales came to roughly $128.6 million in 2022, and retail sales reached about $268 million, or $17,724 for each resident. For a seller, that background matters mostly at the margins: buyers who want a getaway near Saginaw Bay and buyers who need a year-round home bring different budgets.

  • Adults 25 and older with a high school diploma or higher: 88.2 percent.
  • Adults 25 and older with a bachelor's degree or higher: 16.0 percent.
  • Persons in poverty: 11.7 percent.
  • Per capita income: $32,082 in 2024 dollars.

faqs.q: How do I contact the Arenac County deeds office by phone?
faqs.a: The office lists (989) 846-9201 on its web page. Call that line with questions about recording, transfer tax or the online records subscription.

faqs.q: What does Arenac County charge to file a deed?
faqs.a: A deed pays $30.00 whatever its length. A paper that assigns or discharges more than one instrument adds $3.00 for each one beyond the first.

faqs.q: What are the Arenac County transfer tax rates?
faqs.a: The county takes 55 cents per $500 and the state takes $3.75 per $500, rounded up for a partial block. A transfer worth $100 or more owes both unless the deed states an exemption.

faqs.q: Do I have to put the sale price on the deed?
faqs.a: Not if you file a real estate valuation affidavit instead. There is no fee for the affidavit, and the deed must say that one is being filed.

faqs.q: Where can I look at old Arenac County deed books?
faqs.a: Deed books 1 through 214 can be viewed on RECORDhub with a subscription plan from the county. Documents from 1992 forward are on the county's online records site.
